comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C2, C28-C35 regarding muting experiments. Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED with strong endorsement. OpenEval emphasizes statistical rigor and converging evidence, while peer reviewers highlight the innovative experimental approach and technical difficulty. Both conclude that motor practice is required and covert planning is insufficient.

Perfect agreement on claims C48-C56 comparing WNd and dLO groups. Both rate as SUPPORTED and identify this as the central novel finding. OpenEval emphasizes the critical experimental design controlling for mismatch experience, while peer reviewers call it 'surprising and important' with strong behavioral evidence supporting the planning mechanism.

Perfect agreement on claims C24, C126-C131 regarding differential recovery of pitch versus duration. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval focuses on statistical evidence and methodological justification, while peer reviewers accept this as supporting the choice to focus on pitch without substantive challenge.

Perfect agreement on claims C67-C71 addressing alternative explanations. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the logical argument ruling out somatosensory explanations, while peer reviewers acknowledge the reasoning that distinguishes planned changes from reinforcement-learning-guided practice, with minor caveats about training paradigm confounds.

Agreement on claims C72-C74, C77 regarding the two-stage theoretical framework. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to speculative nature, while peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, treating it as reasonable extrapolation. Both acknowledge the framework is consistent with data but requires further testing for broader applicability claims.

Agreement on claims C79-C93 integrating LMAN function literature. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting plausible but speculative mechanisms, while peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, explicitly endorsing the reinterpretation of neural mechanisms. Both recognize this as valuable contextualization rather than direct empirical findings.

Perfect agreement on claims C94-C100 contextualizing findings within motor learning literature. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes appropriate citations and convergent evidence, while peer reviewers implicitly accept the contextualization as providing useful behavioral constraints for future studies.

Strong agreement on claims C4-C5, C62-C66 synthesizing main conclusions about the two-stage model. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes converging evidence from multiple experimental paradigms (7 of 8 claims overlap), while peer reviewers highlight this as identifying a 'previously uncharacterized capacity' with convincing evidence. Peer result includes C3 which OpenEval addresses separately in R4.

Strong agreement on claims C37-C47 regarding deafening experiments and auditory experience necessity. Both rate as SUPPORTED (9 of 11 claims overlap). OpenEval emphasizes robust evidence from two independent paradigms, while peer reviewers accept findings with caveats about interpretation, noting training paradigm confounds affect interpretation but not core observations. Peer result excludes C37-C38 from OpenEval's set.

Strong agreement on claims C58-C61 regarding statistical modeling of planning limits. Both rate as SUPPORTED (4 of 5 claims overlap). OpenEval emphasizes rigorous mixed-effects modeling, while peer reviewers note authors 'suitably addressed confusion about statistical methods' after revision. OpenEval includes C3 which peer reviewers address in R5.

Moderate agreement on claims C101-C109 regarding broader implications. OpenEval rates C101-C106 (human vocal learning parallels) as UNCERTAIN, noting speculative nature requiring validation. Peer reviewers rate C101-C109 as SUPPORTED, treating comparative discussion as reasonable speculation with broad relevance. Peer result combines human parallels (C101-C106) with evolutionary implications (C107-C109) that OpenEval separates into R12.

Partial overlap on claims C107-C109 regarding evolutionary/ethological implications. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting speculative nature of honest signaling and social cohesion hypotheses. Peer reviewers include these claims in their broader R11 evaluation rated as SUPPORTED, treating them as reasonable speculation within the context of broader relevance to vocal and motor learning fields.

OpenEval evaluated claims C110-C125 describing experimental methods and subjects as SUPPORTED, noting clear documentation, appropriate sample sizes, and sound experimental design. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these methodological claims specifically, though methods were implicitly accepted through approval of results.

OpenEval evaluated claims C132-C139 regarding prior literature on pitch versus duration recovery as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate citations and quantitative comparisons. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing this literature synthesis, though it supports the methodological choice evaluated in both R6 results.
